exposure: Birth location (within regional centres 'inborn' vs outside regional centres 'outborn')
outcome: Survival to 1 year without major morbidity
cohort: The study included 1626 liveborn extremely preterm infants in Sweden from 22+0 to 26+6 weeks of gestation, born during 2004-2007 and 2014-2016.
finding: Centralisation of extremely preterm births was associated with a lower 1-year mortality in 2014-2016 compared to 2004-2007, primarily due to a decrease in deaths before 24 hours among infants born within regional centres.
